trade.line: Going down? Rent a tank, grab the kit.

say: Going down? You'll want the kit.
Back from the deep, {name}?

deep.say: Caves under the river. Glints in the walls. Wear the goggles or you'll see nothing.

job.say: Bring me one piece of sea glass from the river caves. I'll make it worth your while.

paid.say: Beautiful. Here, bait for your trouble.

trade.line: Nets, jars, cages and glasses. I buy every butterfly and bird you bring me, and I teach what I know.

say: Wings and feathers, that's my trade.
Ah, a fellow watcher of small things.

opts.t: HOW DO I CATCH A BIRD?

birds.say: Patience and seed. Scatter it, stand still, and they come to you. Take a handful, first one's free.

trade.line: A blade for every purse. Hold P to block; catch the blow on the beat and they stagger.

fight.say: Hold P to block. Catch the blow on the beat and they stagger. Then strike.

say: Cloud coats. Light as weather.
Still cold out there, {name}?

opts.t: IS IT REALLY MADE OF CLOUDS?

cloud.say: Of course. Caught them myself, on the high roofs. Wear it and you'll float a little.

trade.line: Plate for the road. Catch me in the holodeck if you want to train.

train.say: Find me in the holodeck, at the back of the arcade. I do not go easy.

who.say: Just Teddy. I sit here and watch the market go by. Nobody ever asks.

trade.line: Jars by the register. A dollar is a dollar.
One for the next showing? The times are on the screen behind me.
Grown, not made. She wants to rise; you only have to stand on her.

say: She wants to rise.
Back for another, {name}?

wood.say: Somewhere light. It grew reaching up. It still is.

ride.say: Hold her, click, step on. Lean where you want to go. Space to hop. Don't meet a wall fast.

trade.line: (the little one) He fixed them. They work. Mostly.

say: (the little one) He says hi. He doesn't, but he would.
(the little one) Careful, that one's live.

modem.say: (the little one) Put it by a computer at home. It calls the market board. You can order things. Things come.

trade.line: Shh. Shh. ...Okay. What.

say: Shh. Shh. ...Okay. What.
You're loud. Everybody's loud.

hear.say: Two from the precinct walk the street. Guards downstairs. Hold a scanner and you'll hear them too. What you do with that is your business.

box.say: You hear better when you don't look.

trade.line: Nothing illegal, dear. Just inconvenient.

say: Someone's wronged you. I can tell.
Back again. Who is it this time?

golem.say: Big, slow, very tidy minds. Give one rats and it forgets everything else. Walk on by, dear.

trade.line: Every side one colour. Simple. Go on.

say: Hold still. You'd look better in teal.
Click. Click. Click. Oh, you.

how.say: Drag a face to turn its row. Drag the dark to look round. Every side one colour and you're done. I'm fast. You won't be.

trade.line: Up is easy. Down is the trick.

say: Up is easy. Down is the trick.
You again. Still walking? Tsk.

how.say: Hold it and it lifts you. Over the fence, over the river, over anything that bites. Not over houses, dear, houses are tall. Two minutes of air, then down you go, gently.

trade.line: Fresh from far away!

say: Fresh from far away!
Ooh, a customer. Mind the umbrella.

how.say: A pot, a bag of dirt, a seed, and rain. Set the pot down at home, fill it, plant it, water it. It only grows while it's wet. Eat what it gives you and you'll mend.

trade.line: Lamps, tonics, plate. All you need for down below.

say: Lamps, tonics, plate. All you need for down below.
Goggles on, wick trimmed. What'll it be?

why.say: Down there the dust gets in your eyes. Up here the sun does. Can't win.

trade.line: A tonic for every worry.

say: Tonics brewed under a full moon. Mostly.
A ward for every worry.

ward.say: A promise the dark has to keep. Strength, sharp eyes, a cure for the spiders' bite.

trade.line: Slime in a bottle? I'll take it.

say: Slime in a bottle? I'll take it. Don't ask what for.
Everything from down there is worth something to someone.

skull.say: He was a skeleton guard. Now he's a conversation piece.

trade.line: Steel remembers what you teach it.

say: Steel remembers what you teach it.
The orb hums. It likes you. Or it's hungry.

orb.say: It sings into the steel until the steel sings back. An enchanted blade bites deeper.

trade.line: Breathe. Then strike.

say: Breathe. Then strike.
Even a shark must learn to walk.

land.say: The lake was too small for me. The keep was not.

trade.line: Spar with me! Please?

say: Spar with me! Please? Nobody spars with me.
I'm going to be captain one day.

cap.say: Captain Voss says I need to grow first. I'm growing. Slowly.

say: Hurt? Come here. Hold still.
Leaf and root. It mends what the dark breaks.

herbs.say: Things that grow in the park and nowhere else. Bring me back alive and I'll use them on you.

say: Ash and ember, {name}. The keep pays for what you put down below.
Sit a while. Or take some work.

board.say: Pick one. The keep keeps count; I pay on the count.

took.say: Then go. The stair is that way. Come back up when it's done.

say: Sit, if you like. The fire's for everyone.
I have watched that stair longer than the park has had a wall.

under.say: Halls that go down further than anyone has counted. Slime, spiders, the bones of old guards. Each level worse than the last.

shut.say: We keep it watched. Shut is not something a stair can be.

who.say: The keep. Mice, owls, frogs, whoever comes. The park is ours to guard. Every section has its stair; this one is ours.

say: Whoooo... are you?
Ask me something. I may even answer.

opts.t: HOW DO I LIVE LONGER DOWN THERE?

a1.say: Deeper is darker, darker is meaner. The stairs down are always at the far end.

a2.say: Webs hold. Lava burns. Spikes come up in turns: count, then step.

a3.say: The golden one walks the deep halls. Fell it and Old Ember will make you rich.

say: Every level drawn. Every trap marked. Mostly.
Lost? No. Just not yet found.

map.say: One hall per level, longer every time. Up stair at your back, down stair at the far end. Torches the only light.

say: Been down to the third. Wouldn't go further without a friend.
The spiders are thicker deeper. So are the webs.

saw.say: Three to five of them each level, never the same. Slimes up top, spiders and guards below. They notice you sooner the deeper you go.

say: The keep stands. As long as I do, it stands.
Report anything that crawls. Anything.

need.say: Hands. Swords. Old Ember pays bounties by the fire outside the gate.

run.say: The Elder decides. I enforce. The rest of them do as they like, mostly.

trade.line: Bring me gems. I pay fair.

say: Stones from every corner of the park. And under it.
Bring me gems. I pay better than the golems. Mostly.

q.say: The golems' cave, the deep halls, the Hudson's bed. Bring me what you find.

trade.line: Rocks are just slow gems.

say: Rocks are just slow gems.
Seen anything sparkle? Tell me first.

trade.line: Moss ale's fresh. Food's hot.

say: What'll it be? Moss ale's fresh.
Sit. Eat. Don't start anything.

q.say: The Mossy Flagon. Every guard in the keep drinks here after the night watch.

trade.line: Bait's a dollar. Patience is free.

say: The lake gives. You just have to wait.
Bait's a dollar. Patience is free.

q.say: Out past the reeds, where the brook runs in. At dusk.

trade.line: Feet first. Then the blade.

say: Feet first. Then the blade.
Again. Until you don't think.

q.say: Cuts on the pells, arrows at the butts. Real steel, real wood. Watch them.

trade.line: Light for the lost.

say: ...the dead sleep easier when I pass.
Light for the lost. Even you.

trade.line: Nice. No. Let me fix that.

say: Nice. No. Let me fix that.
You again. Better. Not there yet.

from.say: Earth makes the best clothes in the galaxy. Nobody out there knows how to fade denim. I buy it by the crate.

trade.line: "PICK ME." "NO, ME." "GET US OUT OF HERE."
Patience. And water.
A map. Folded the way the roots run.

say: Sit. Once, before the city...
Ah. Lost again? Sit.
Once, before the city, this was all one tree. The streets are where its roots ran. That's why they bend.
Once, a man tried to map the market without me. He's still in the park somewhere. Wave if you see him.
Once, the lake was a puddle a giant stepped in. He said sorry. Nobody heard him.
Once, the subway was a rabbit hole. The rabbits moved out when the trains came. They live under the bodega now.

trade.line: Bad day? Smoke it off.

say: Bad day? Smoke it off.
Evening. It's always evening somewhere.

blue.say: Rolled where the sky stays that colour all day. Smoke's blue too. Lasts longer.

trade.line: Who are we calling? Not her. I won't.

say: Who are we calling? Not her. I won't.
Hold, please. ...Yes? You.

how.say: Call any shop in the city. They'll bring it round. The big one goes in your pocket. Well. A big pocket.

say: Wanna be someone else for a minute?
I've got a pigeon's whole morning on here. Don't ask how.
Got a run if you've got legs.
Every drain in this city goes somewhere. Most go somewhere worse.
This one comes out in '94. Good ending.
Some films get made everywhere. Same film, every planet. Weird, right?
Heavy? Let it walk.
My bag's been following me for years. I think it likes me.
Oh! You can see me. How embarrassing.
I can't carry anything, you know. I just like to look.
...blub.
It's warm in here. You should try a bubble.
Soil's different up by the lake. Sweeter.
Been walking since the spores were young.
Time? I've got some. Not much.
Tick. Tock. Sorry. Habit.

trade.line: Hives, smoke and jars. I buy honey and wax, and I'll teach you to keep them.

say: Slow hands, calm bees.
Mind the smoke. It's for them, not you.

how.say: Set a hive on the lawn where the flowers are thick. Come back in an hour or so with empty jars. Smoke them first, and wear a veil. The flowers near the hive make the honey: clover, lavender, sunflower, rose. And by night, deep in the park, once in a while... moon honey.

trade.line: Hot off the cart. Cold out of the box.

say: Hot off the cart. Cold out of the box.
Back again, {name}? Usual?

q.say: Meat. Probably. It's a market, friend.

job.title: THE CART MAN, HOT DOG CART

trade.line: Picked this morning. Somewhere.

say: Picked this morning. Somewhere.
Squeeze it, you bought it.

q.say: The park's trees, mostly. Don't tell the squirrel.

trade.line: Odds and ends. Mostly ends.

say: Odds and ends. Mostly ends.
Everything here was somebody's once.

opts.t: WHERE DO YOU GET IT ALL?

q.say: Attics, alleys, the river at low tide. Don't ask which.

trade.line: Anything with a value, I'll take it. Half now. Someone pays full later.

say: It all works. Some of it on purpose.
No refunds. No questions. No warranty.

q.say: Plug it in and find out. That's the fun.

trade.line: Seeds, pots, a little dirt. Grow something.

say: Seeds, pots, a little dirt. Grow something.
Your windowsill looks lonely, {name}.

q.say: Hum seeds. They grow anywhere and they sing a little.

job.title: THE FLOWER LADY, SEEDS AND POTS
DOORMAN, TICKETS WITH THE TICKET FOX

trade.line: Jackets, jeans, coats, shades. Try it on.
Wine, chocolates, or something with bubbles. Quick, the bell's about to go.
Canvases and paper. I buy good paintings and old things.
Dog food, cat food, apples for the grazers. Feed them a little every day.
Bacon egg and cheese, salt pepper ketchup. That's the law.
Wood, wheels, bearings, and the ones that float.
Buy an implant here, then sit in the chair and I fit it. One to a slot; I take them out too.

standing_worker_on_a_call.name: THE STANDING WORKER ON A CALL

trade.line: Nets and jars. I buy every butterfly you bring me, and I teach what I know.
Nets, seed, feeders and glasses; I buy the birds you bring me. Climbing? Three points on the rungs: practise on the fire escapes.

job.title: FLIES A KITE ON THE LAWN

trade.line: Hives, smoke and jars. I buy honey and wax, and I'll teach you to keep them.
Rods, reels, bait; a tank, goggles and a headlight for down below. I buy what you land.
Fish food for the tanks.
Stones? We buy stones. Every one you bring. And a good light for the dark.

holidaymaker_in_a_sun_hat.name: THE HOLIDAYMAKER IN A SUN HAT

child_with_a_painted_face.name: THE CHILD WITH A PAINTED FACE

trade.line: Fresh fruit and honey on the house. Well, not on the house.
Tickets for the rides and the games. A strip of five is cheaper at the booth window.
A blade for every purse. Hold P to block; catch the blow on the beat and they stagger.

kid_in_a_bedsheet_ghost_costume.name: THE KID IN A BEDSHEET GHOST COSTUME

kid_in_a_black_cat_costume.name: THE KID IN A BLACK CAT COSTUME

kid_in_a_caped_hero_costume.name: THE KID IN A CAPED HERO COSTUME

kid_in_a_cardboard_robot_costume.name: THE KID IN A CARDBOARD ROBOT COSTUME

kid_in_a_pumpkin_costume.name: THE KID IN A PUMPKIN COSTUME

kid_in_a_skeleton_suit.name: THE KID IN A SKELETON SUIT

trade.line: Wood, wheels, bearings, and the ones that float.

say: Need a board?
Back for another, {name}?

ride.say: Hold it, click, step on. Push to go, lean to turn, space to ollie. Ramps and the bowl are all yours.

trade.line: Ale, stout, or the cola. I don't do cocktails. I don't do umbrellas.

say: What'll it be?
Keep it down, the octopus is counting.

opts.t: HOW LONG HAVE YOU WORKED HERE?

long.say: Since before the stairs. I dug them.

say: BEEP. TICKETS IN, PRIZES OUT.
WIN AT SKEE-BALL. BRING ME TICKETS. BEEP.

what.say: A RING IS 4 TICKETS. A YO-YO IS 8. THE BEAR IS 20. DOUBLE-CLICK THE COUNTER.

trade.line: Popcorn's fresh. Nachos are... warm. Don't feed the screen.

say: Snacks for the show?
Butter on that? There's always butter.

now.say: Whatever's on the board behind the fox. I only see the backs of heads.

say: Hoo goes there? Oh. A visitor.
No flash. No touching. No climbing the mammoth.

opts.t: WHAT IS THERE TO DO HERE?

do.say: Read the plaques. Then the curator at the desk will quiz you, a dollar a right answer. The fish tank's in the Earth gallery; bring fish food.

sleep.say: In the day, with one eye open. The meteorite has tried to leave twice.

trade.line: Every sale keeps the mammoth dusted.

say: Something to remember us by?
The plush mammoth is very soft. Softer than the real one.
Welcome to the art museum!
My tours take the ground floor: a painting at a time.

how.say: Three dollars at my sign, then follow me. I stop at each painting and tell you about it. Double-click one to see it up close.

fav.say: The Van Gogh upstairs. It has its own tour: open it and press GUIDED TOUR.

say: Next, please. Deposits, withdrawals, no dragons.
The account pays a little every day. Don't ask about the gold at the back.

how.say: Put money in at either cage. It earns one in a hundred a day, up to fifty dollars, and it's kept for you.

trade.line: Fresh from far away!
Bring me what grows in the dark.
Fists up. Again.

say: Fists up, {name}. The golems and what crawls below need thinning.
Take a bounty, or a lesson.

board.say: Pick one. I keep the count from my tower; I pay on the count.

took.say: Then go. The stair is that way. Come back up when it's done.

trade.line: Flounder, blues, bass, off the boats this morning. Bring me what you land, I pay better than the shed.
Pan fish, cats and eels, by the piece. You fish? I buy, and I pay market price.
Blue crabs by the bushel, live. Got crabs of your own? Put them on the scale.
The big fish get cut here. Sturgeon, bass: I take all you can carry.
